range.why: The base is a TAG, not the branch name `main`: a branch name moves and a gate keyed on one silently changes what it compares. `aw-modularize-base` is the upstream tip this series was carried onto, so `base..HEAD` is exactly the commits the series ADDS. `aw-pre-merge` stays the monolith the parity gates compare content against, and the window's branch point.

identity.why: ANCHORED, never written down. The expected identity is read at runtime from a published non-merge commit inside the base's history (the base merge's second parent), whose author must equal its committer -- so the series can never vouch for itself, and a literal name or address (operator data, R-LOC-03; and the one field a maintainer could widen to two entries) still has nowhere to go. A stray identity can only be cleared by removing it from history.

window.why: Pinned by VALUE to the range's real earliest author date and asserted equal to it, so widening this bound to admit an out-of-window commit reddens on the other side. The end is deliberately NOT pinned: `today` is the bound (a commit dated tomorrow is a broken clock or a forgery), because an end date pinned by value must be re-stamped by the very commit that lands the stamp. The branch POINT is declared separately from the range base because the series kept its real dates when it was carried onto a later upstream tip; it must be an ancestor of the base, so it cannot be moved back to widen the window.

count.why: A floor with NO ceiling. The series may grow -- tasks 83 onward still commit -- but a range that holds fewer commits than this has lost history to a squash, a reset or a dropped branch, which is the failure a count can actually detect. The plan's pre-execution estimate of 70-80 commits was superseded by the loop authoring one commit per closed task as the work happened.
